classes.name: irreversible-custody-and-external-state
classes.definition: Tasks that initialize or mint an immutable launch, change hook claim or fee behavior, move or account for USDG, create a signable transaction, change an Operations signer, decode provider transactions, mutate a provider, bridge assets, purchase or sell a card, freeze eligibility, broadcast a payout, or alter journal and custody recovery.

classes.name: authority-binding-and-release-truth
classes.definition: Tasks that define deployment-manifest membership, provider admission, fee-policy interpretation, policy limits, interface truth, chain evidence, runtime hashes, launchEligible, release gates, or any boundary that can permit or prevent an R4 action.

classes.name: deterministic-read-only-support
classes.definition: Tasks proven unable to move assets, create a signable action, mutate a journal, grant authority, or determine release readiness, such as isolated formatters and non-authoritative projections.

classes.name: documentary-presentation-only
classes.definition: Timeless explanatory documentation that cannot change executable behavior, authority, deployment membership, interface truth, or release state.

moduleDefaults.reason: The boundary decides whether a future money path is in scope.
Provider facts and fee policy decide whether launch can proceed.
The manifest determines the production runtime set and excludes the legacy custody family.
Roles control claims, pauses, limit changes, and Operations rotation.
Issuance and token behavior are irreversible.
Callback authentication and initialization govern immutable market and fee mutation.
Gross fee accounting changes shared-custody liabilities.
Process claims and rotation control money movement.
Atomic pool initialization, Permit2 funding, and custody binding are irreversible.
The frozen code remains high-risk even though deployment is forbidden.
The repository controls durable money-mutation state and restart safety.
Transaction decoding and signer policy gate all external asset actions.
Caps, holds, canaries, and kill switches control whether money action is possible.
The runner performs the irreversible stages and custody attribution.
A pre-claim snapshot fixes the direct-payout recipient set.
Per-recipient transfers and finality determine irreversible holder payments.
The signer boundary controls external transaction authority.
Readiness and evidence can permit or deny a future live action.

highRiskTaskKinds: onchain source, storage, ABI, event, initialization, claim control, or deployment
fee formula, gross-up, remainder, liability conservation, token transfer, or reentrancy
Operations claim window, Treasury limit change, pause, rotation, custody binding, or direct payout
provider binding, transaction allowlist, semantic decoder, signer boundary, or finality rule
bridge, Collector mutation, card hold, buyback, return attribution, or external broadcast
journal, fencing, recovery, typed amount, custody ledger, snapshot, or payout manifest
deployment manifest, release evidence, readiness gate, external authorization, or live evidence
classificationRules: Every task starts at its module default class.
Anything the owner marks high is R4 regardless of diff size or apparent reversibility.
A task spanning modules uses the highest class touched.
Any asset movement, liability mutation, immutable deployment, transaction construction, signing, broadcast, spend, or payout-data compilation is R4.
Any binding, policy, proof, finality, or readiness condition that can permit or block an R4 action is at least R3.
R2 or R1 applies only after the task is proven isolated from custody, authority, deployment membership, release truth, and signable action preparation.
An unresolved provider, custody, or authorization fact fails closed and never lowers the risk class.
doubtLoopExit: No plausible unresolved critical or high loss, overcharge, unfunded liability, duplicate action, wrong-custody, double-payment, signer escalation, false readiness, or forbidden legacy-runtime deployment remains without executable falsification evidence.
